newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Albania PM says south under authorities' control.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM says south under authorities' control.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino said in an interview published on Monday that the state had regained control of much of the impoverished Balkan country's lawless southern region.
"The situation has improved, local authorities have the situation under control. Many (rebel) committees have been dissolved and the authorities taken charge," Fino told Austrian daily Die Presse.
Fino's Socialists joined President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party in an all-party emergency government last month.

More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured during a wave of violent unrest and near-anarchy that has swept the country after the collapse of a row of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes in January.
The country's south, where army weapons depots were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts, has been the focus of the violence and several towns were taken over by rebels.
Fino added his government would do all it can to ensure early nationwide elections could go ahead in late June as planned.

"We will take all measures so that the elections can take place at the planned date. The government is cooperating with all political forces, together we want to destroy all the elements that want to prevent free elections," he said.
